points.description: States that a variable is a location in memory (storage space in the computer). Equivalent wording such as 'a named place in memory' or 'a memory location' earns the mark. Saying it is only a label or name, with no reference to memory or storage, does not earn this mark.
States that this location can store a value (data), or that the stored value can change or be changed. Equivalent wording such as 'holds data' or 'contains a value' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for a answer that says a variable is a memory location and that it stores a value, in any equivalent wording. Award 3 for the memory-location idea alone and 2 for the storing-a-value idea alone, with no partial credit within each point. Do not require the phrase 'named' or any extra detail such as data types or addresses.
